BMP is a potent inducer of cranial bone regeneration, that BMP-induced bone regeneration requires bone marrow stroma, that BMP induces bone formation by a process of cell differentiation, and that the target for BMP is the perivascuar connective tissue cells of the bone.
BMP-induced bone regeneration of a 14-mm calvarial defect in the adult dog is complete when bone marrow is included in the graft.
BMP induces complete repair of a 14-mm calvarial defect in the dog, and that the target cell for BMP is the connective tissue cell of the marrow stroma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the induction of cranial bone regeneration in the dog by bone morphogenetics proteins (BMP) and the molecular mechanism of the process.
the molecular mechanisms of bone morphogenetic proteins and their target cells, the perivascular cells in bone marrow stroma, and their differentiation into osteoprogenitors and osteoblasts.
the molecular basis of osteogenesis, and the goal is to develop a bone morphogenetic gene therapy for repair of bone defects in humans
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BMP-induced calvarial repair is a process of bone marrow stroma cell differentiation into osteoprogenitors and osteoblasts.
BMP induces bone regeneration in the adult dog by stimulating differentiation of bone marrow stroma cells, which are the target of BMP in the adult dog.
bone marrow is the source of cells for calvarial bone formation and BMP is the inducer of differentiation of these cells into osteoblasts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BMP is a potent inducer of cranial bone regeneration, but the target cell is not the osteoblast, but the osteoprogenitor cell, and that this target cell is a pericyte.
bone morphogenetic proteins induce bone regeneration by inducing differentiation of perivascular connectives cells of the host bone marrow stroma.
the bone morphogenetic proteins (BMPs), a family of growth factors that are members of the TGF-β superfamily, are the most potent known inducers of bone regeneration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bone marrow stoma, including the endosteum, is an important source of osteoprogenitor stem cells in bone healing and repair.
the calvaria is not the most favorable site for BMP-induced bone regeneration.
BMP is a powerful bone regenerative agent that may be used to repair large cranial defects and other bone defects.
